findings: Concurrent scan race condition — if two scans run simultaneously (an attacker POSTs /api/admin/videos/scan twice), the last save wins and earlier progress may be lost. The frontend prevents double-clicks, but the server doesn't check isScanning before starting a new scan. Add a server-side mutex or check the flag before starting.

Scan still makes O(anime_count) episode-fetch requests — the scan loops over every anime and calls /admin/anime/${anime.id}/episodes one by one (batched in groups of 50). For 1,000 anime this is 1,000 requests instead of 10–20 bulk /admin/episodes calls. Batching improves wall-clock time but doesn't fix the design. Use the backend's bulk episode list endpoint if available.

No test coverage — videoHealthService.ts, videoSourceFinder.ts, and the five API routes have no test files. Add unit tests for URL validation (HEAD timeout, 403 fallback to GET, network errors), integration tests for scan pagination and store persistence, and mock tests for the auto-repair flow.
